customer_ops: Hey team — we're seeing intermittent SSE disconnects from the API in prod, specifically using our Go client. Clients often reconnect and get a short partial completion then another resume fragment, which looks like duplicated tokens in our downstream processor. Also noticed an unexpected spike in tokens billed for those sessions.

maria_s: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste a minimal repro and any logs?

customer_ops: Minimal repro (Go, net/http + http2):
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 60*time.Second)
defer cancel()
req, _ := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, "GET", "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=...", nil)
req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer TOKEN")
resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
// iterate SSE lines and feed to parser
```
Logs show: `client closed connection (499)` then later a reconnect that yields a tail fragment like `...ing.` and then another resume fragment `...ng.` (overlap).

devlin_r: Can you share the exact SDK version? Are you using the Go helper or rolling your own SSE parser?

customer_ops: We're using our own simple SSE parser on top of net/http. SDK not involved, but behavior matches what we saw when testing the new go-sdk (v0.14.2) — same reconnection resume behavior.

support-bot: :rotating_light: Incident alert: increased SSE reconnect rate for region us-west-2 (5xx spike + partial-frame reports)

alex_k: Interesting — this sounds like a resume/race where the server-side resume accepts an offset but the client double-sends the last chunk. Could be a client-side abort/cleanup ordering issue when context cancels. Do you have an example trace (request ids)?

customer_ops: Example trace ids: req=rcp_01G1, resume_token=rtkn_9e7ab, timestamps attached: 2024-06-25T16:40:12Z -> 499; reconnect at 16:40:13Z; partial fragment at 16:40:13.112Z; second fragment at 16:40:13.241Z.

maria_s: Also seeing billing anomalies correlated with those resumes in our logs — some sessions counted tokens twice when a resume produced overlapping fragments.

ryan_t: Repro steps I ran locally with a small script that cancels context mid-stream: yields same overlap when the client cancels then immediately reconnects. Minimal test: start stream, after first token set cancel ctx, then new ctx.Do(req) -> resumed response includes last 10 bytes from previous plus new bytes.

alex_k: Can you paste sanitized raw frames (SSE event lines) from the failing session? Even a short excerpt helps.

customer_ops: raw frames:
```
event: data
data: {"id":"tok_...","text":"...end"}

# client cancels (499)

# reconnect
event: data
data: {"id":"tok_...","text":"...end"}
event: data
data: {"id":"tok_...","text":"ing."}
```

devlin_r: Thanks. Hypothesis: client cancels mid-chunk -> server completes chunk and buffers it for resume. Our resume path may re-stream the buffered tail plus continue; if the client still processes buffered suffix from before abort (race), you see overlap/duplication. The billing pipeline currently attributes tokens per event emission, so duplicates count twice in some edge paths.

alex_k: For Go clients specifically, there's a known subtlety: when you cancel the context, net/http may close the underlying connection asynchronously; if your parser hasn't consumed the buffered reader fully, you can observe the tail twice after reconnect. The fix can be either on client (drain and discard on cancel before reconnect) or server (de-duplicate resume tokens server-side / idempotent resume semantics).

maria_s: For triage: can the customer try two mitigations and report back quick numbers?
- A: On cancel, explicitly read until `\n\n` or EOF to drain the response before reconnecting.
- B: Use the published go-sdk v0.14.3-rc with a fix we pushed to delay resume for 50ms to allow connection teardown. PR: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/8672 (internal).

customer_ops: Will try A now; B is internal but we can try the rc if you share it.

support-bot: :white_check_mark: Support note: created support ticket #SUP-8242 and flagged for eng-ml and eng-runtime.

(10m later)
customer_ops: Tried A (drain on cancel) — reconnects no longer show overlapping tokens in 18/20 attempts. Token billing spike also resolved in those test runs.

ryan_t: Good to hear. I reproduced with a small harness and validated drain fixes it.

alex_k: We'll push a small server-side guard too: idempotent resume token check to suppress re-emitting the last N bytes if the resumed client reports the same last-seen-id. That should handle non-draining clients. I'll open a follow-up PR for runtime.

devlin_r: Action items:
- eng-runtime: implement resume idempotency (PR queued)
- devex: add guidance in Go streaming best-practices: drain on cancel + using SDK helper that handles this.
- support: patch billing pipeline to ignore duplicate resume-fingerprint for 24h window while we roll out.

maria_s: ETA on runtime PR?

alex_k: Drafted PR, running unit tests now. Targeting canary deploy tomorrow EOD. PR link (internal): https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/8689

customer_ops: Thanks everyone — will keep watching. Appreciate the quick triage. :thumbsup:

devlin_r: For note: this thread shows an important cross-layer gap (client connection lifecycle vs server resume semantics) — capturing as a postmortem if we see customer impact at scale.

support-bot: :hammer_and_wrench: Ticket #SUP-8242 updated: mitigation applied, awaiting canary results.

maria_s: Closing loop: if anyone else sees similar, ask them to include raw SSE event excerpts + whether they drain on cancel.

customer_ops: Will follow up if it resurfaces. Thanks again.
